summary: Public demo repository containing a complete, real walkthrough of the runx local quickstart with the sealed receipt committed as evidence.
audience: developers evaluating governed runtimes for agent skills; newcomers wanting to see exactly what the sealed-receipt flow produces before installing
observations: Ran the documented quickstart on Ubuntu 24.04 + Node v20.18.1 with @runxhq/cli 0.9.1: `runx skill ./examples/hello-world -i message='hello, runx' --json` returned runx.skill_run.v1 with status sealed and receipt_id sha256:e6b05ab4eebc97ad5ba36abe64ccca8c2141e3170f7099847fd2a89ba9435b47 in under a second.
RUNX_RECEIPT_DIR is honored consistently by runx skill, runx history, and runx verify: receipts and index.json land in the chosen directory and are discoverable from it.

runx history <receipt-id> --detail --json returns a runx.receipt_inspection.v1 projection showing authority, decisions, acts, and seal summary; unsigned local receipts honestly report verification.status unverified.

runx verify refuses unsigned receipts by default and requires RUNX_RECEIPT_VERIFY_KID + RUNX_RECEIPT_VERIFY_ED25519_PUBLIC_KEY_BASE64 or an explicit --allow-local-development-signatures flag; with the flag the demo receipt verifies ok.
The repo links runx.ai, github.com/runxhq/runx, and the npm package, and commits the actual sealed runx.receipt.v1 receipt as sealed-receipt.json so readers can inspect a real artifact.
venue_rule: A personal public GitHub repository is the operator's own demo artifact, explicitly listed by the bounty as an acceptable action type (a relevant repo/demo/README/example that mentions runx).
